fences.title: Bunny is the healthy-path portrait accelerator
fences.decision: Healthy browser tabs load content-addressed portrait and requested labelled-card bytes directly from Bunny. The extension starts one browser-native Bunny image and, only while the tab is undecided and Bunny remains unresolved for 350 ms, starts the canonical first-party image as a bounded hedge; the first decoded source becomes the tab decision. The 2.5 second source timeout remains a ceiling, not a serial pre-fallback delay. The first-party Worker uses one server-side portrait-storage adapter and treats authenticated Storage and the public CDN as distinct regional views of the same immutable key; only failure of every configured view is missing. Website Ops records split-view success distinctly and exposes operator-triggered, bounded rechecks for verdicts older than 30 days. Country is not connectivity: working Vietnamese providers and VPNs use Bunny too. The owner's paid Bunny service is the chosen alternative to unavailable R2; R2 enablement or a Cloudflare paid upgrade is not a prerequisite.
fences.reason: Direct Bunny delivery avoids charging every healthy portrait or labelled-card read to the Cloudflare Worker budget. A resolver failure on one network is the reason the fallback exists, not evidence that Bunny should be disabled globally. CASP8AP2 proved the inverse black swan: the full image loaded through an American VPN while the Vietnam first-party Storage read returned 404, so neither one successful region nor one failed provider view establishes global object truth.
fences.change_control: Retiring or replacing Bunny, changing the 350 ms bounded hedge, returning worker-buffered data URLs to the normal hot path, changing server-side read order, or adding a provider-specific read path requires an explicit architecture migration that updates this registry, the delivery runbook, the single storage adapter, source policy, production and staging configuration, behavioral tests, and deploy guard in one reviewed change. Regional incidents must preserve separate evidence for client DNS, first-party delivery, authenticated Storage, and CDN replica visibility. Canonical first-party identity does not prohibit Bunny caching public immutable metadata. Byte-equivalent caches are permitted; private or mutable APIs must never enter that public cache. Any metadata acceleration cutover must prove actual CDN HITs, cold-miss and fallback costs, snapshot coherence, and independent portrait/detail progress before being reported shipped.

fences.title: Gene discovery is eligibility-gated and range-stable
fences.decision: Complete canonical profiles are indexable through one shared eligibility predicate, while aliases redirect, incomplete profiles remain noindex, unknown symbols return 404, and the crawlable archive uses frozen self-locating prefix ranges rather than numeric pages. The canonical public machine image is the Iconoplasm gene blot, not its source portrait. A blot is the exact shared image-only card composition: published portrait cover crop, protection gradient, full gene name at bottom left, and gene symbol at bottom right. The exact versioned published card selected by KV_GALLERY_VERSION owns every input from which the renderer fingerprint and immutable object key are deterministically derived. Only a workstation may render the 768x1024 WebP from the gallery's 384x512 CSS artboard at 2x device density; it persists exact bytes locally before uploading to Bunny, while Cloudflare serves but never renders them. Blot-only materialization performs zero KV writes. Zero-KV corpus uploads enter gene image sitemaps through bounded exact-symbol reads of the D1 materialization ledger; every returned row must match the selected card's portrait SHA, renderer fingerprint, dimensions, and immutable key, so D1 proves readiness without selecting image identity or scanning the ledger. When an eligible gene has a ready blot, its page exposes that blot as a server-rendered img with alt text inside an initially hidden print-copy surface that becomes visible only after the existing request print copy action. The default page contains no duplicate blot or explanatory caption. Open Graph and Twitter image metadata, one linked WebPage/ImageObject/Gene JSON-LD graph, and the image sitemap preserve independent blot discovery. The stable first-party /blot/{SYMBOL}.webp route derives the current immutable key from the selected card and temporarily falls back only to an exact-card legacy blot while renderer-v2 coverage grows. Bunny is the healthy-region accelerator for non-Vietnam delivery, while the first-party route remains the canonical identity and Vietnam fallback. Blot materialization is never a gene-publication gate: a valid complete card without a ready matching blot remains indexable, linked from its frozen text-only archive range, and listed in its gene-sitemap shard, while only its image-specific projections are absent. Massive range pages never render thumbnails, so discovery does not replace the gallery collection mechanic. A missing requested card or invalid selected artifact fails the affected document or shard with uncached 503. The source portrait remains subordinate. Agent image lookup uses a free bounded POST resolver of at most 50 identifiers over the exact published-card authority and returns only a deterministically resolvable gene_blot. The same resolver feeds the human Diagram Studio and its WebMCP tools: humans and agents edit one visible document, while direct canonical bitmap retrieval remains available for external multimodal work. Studio is a creative surface in the immersive Archive/Clans/Studio switcher, never a second archive or image authority. The temporary /portrait/{SYMBOL}.webp alias was retired after a live exact-card audit proved ready blots for all 19,023 published genes and regional delivery checks passed; immutable /portraits/v1 assets remain available to portrait-native product surfaces but never enter this workflow. /blot/{SYMBOL}.webp is canonical. Published gene portraits and published gene blots are the only two Iconoplasm asset classes dedicated under CC0 1.0 Universal. The visible usage page, resolver permission fields, ready-blot ImageObject license metadata, and raw-image HTTP license links must agree without extending CC0 to catalog data, metadata, prose, software, prompts, unpublished images, services, or other assets. Homepage discovery reuses the existing non-visual description instead of adding visible archive controls. Model-training crawlers are blocked before Worker execution while AI search and user-directed retrieval agents remain allowed.
fences.reason: Search engines and assistant retrieval need one ordinary, named image whose pixels carry Iconoplasm's actual gene ontology. Publishing the raw source portrait as the primary image discards the gene name and symbol and misidentifies the product. A locally rendered immutable blot tied to the exact card epoch keeps visible HTML, social metadata, structured data, archives, public media, and sitemaps on one image identity without introducing Worker rendering or a second portrait-selection timeline. Frozen ranges provide a predictable crawl path, fail-closed readiness prevents partial or stale image documents, and the Bunny-to-first-party delivery split preserves acceleration outside Vietnam without making a provider hostname canonical.

Range boundaries may change only through an explicit biological-inventory migration. Do not promote a raw portrait as the canonical public image; do not reintroduce source-portrait retrieval into the agent gene-image workflow; give human and agent diagram editing separate document models; remove direct canonical bitmap retrieval from WebMCP; broaden CC0 beyond published portraits and published blots; let blot readiness remove a complete gene from its archive or sitemap; render thumbnails on massive gene-range pages; show a duplicate blot by default; add redundant visible SEO caption copy; render a blot inside a Worker; derive a public image from route, discovery, or live D1 portrait state; let a request render, enroll, or repair a blot; emit a partial sitemap; publish a full-corpus image manifest or source-portrait link on every archive row; make Bunny canonical; add the gene archive to the immersive Archive/Clans/Studio switcher; or replace the purpose-specific crawler split with a blanket AI-bot block.

fences.title: Queue wakeups follow durable due times
fences.decision: Cloudflare Queue messages wake durable ledger work only when it is runnable; unfinished future work is delayed until the earliest next_attempt_at and is never polled by immediate replacement messages.
fences.reason: A single future retry otherwise creates an ack/read/delete/send feedback loop that consumes the daily Queue allowance without doing work. Short polling caps also spend retry attempts and can dead-letter a message before its durable backoff expires.
fences.change_control: Queue topology, durable status accounting, retry delays, consumer configuration, behavioral tests, instructions, and the runbook must change atomically. Any replacement must prove a bounded number of billable operations while no work is due.

fences.title: The primary Iconoplasm D1 is bounded operational state
fences.decision: The primary D1 stays below an 80% target of its 500,000,000-byte per-database wall by storing immutable profile prose once, moving publish events older than 30 days to a separately bound cold audit D1 after row-level verification, retaining only one current row plus the newest 100 audit revisions for each administrator recognition policy, and storing recognition validation in one singleton receipt rather than an attempt ledger.
fences.reason: Duplicated manifestation prose and an unbounded 297,818-row publish ledger filled the database and stopped all writes. The old dashboard compared the database to the unrelated 5 GB account allowance, so it reported roughly 10% usage at the per-database hard limit. Administrator policy revisions are operational audit state, not another unbounded event ledger.
fences.change_control: Large payload placement, read-model columns, append-only ledgers, recognition-policy desired rows and 100-revision retention, singleton validation-receipt shape, scheduled KV cleanup ownership, archive bindings, capacity thresholds, observability, migrations, tests, instructions, runbook, and deploy enforcement must change atomically. Cold history may be removed from the hot database only after verified archival; recognition validation attempts must never become retained history, and the default scheduled recognition reconciler must remain the eventual cleanup owner for all three immutable policy namespaces.

fences.title: Fulfillment is one bounded receipt per completed publication, recipient, and gene
fences.decision: A completed generation session has one durable publication identity. Discord delivery waits for each complete publication-recipient-gene group, sends one message with at most ten full-resolution preview images, and links the authoritative gene gallery for the complete result set. The Request inbox mirrors the same durable receipt boundary with a bounded preview mosaic and group-level read acknowledgement.
fences.reason: Request-time button presses are not a meaningful notification boundary. The durable workstation publication is the point where the exact completed images are known. Completion-time or cron-window grouping is still unsafe because it can merge unrelated publications or fragment retries. Discord cannot carry one hundred useful image attachments in one message, and the Worker must keep memory and subrequests bounded.
fences.change_control: Durable publication identity, fulfillment group-size columns, delivery-pending trigger snapshots, group completeness, Discord and Request inbox presentation, group-level read acknowledgement, attachment and memory ceilings, nonce idempotency, reconciliation, workstation payloads, behavioral tests, instructions, and this runbook must change atomically. Never replace the durable publication boundary with timing, row adjacency, or request-time clicks.

fences.title: Iconoplasm is static-first with one dynamic Worker invocation
fences.decision: The Iconoplasm custom hostname is owned directly by the existing stateful Worker, where matching build artifacts are served by Workers Static Assets before Worker execution and dynamic misses enter that Worker exactly once.
fences.reason: On the Free plan, the former wildcard public proxy charged one public and one internal invocation for every request, including more than one hundred static dependencies on a normal page. Asset-first delivery removes static traffic from the Worker quota and direct dynamic routing removes the redundant proxy invocation without changing vote authority or adding a state holder.
fences.change_control: Route ownership, static bundle construction and limits, security headers, rate-limit ownership, stateful bindings, deployment order, tests, instructions, and this runbook must change atomically. A replacement must be selected from current production evidence and prove equal or lower Worker use while preserving complete gene first paint and strongly ordered votes; this fence is not authority by tradition.

fences.title: Anonymous startup and extension hover use the published read plane
fences.decision: Anonymous homepage startup avoids auth, settings, inventory, and admin probes; authenticated startup is gated by a non-authoritative session-presence hint. The visible signed-out archive contains the four fixed published starters INS, RHO, PRL, and CD4; decorative reverse-card continuation is inert markup and never expands the discovery set or triggers reads. Signed-out dossier visits persist across the full 19,023-gene browser-local shelf; an authenticated page session merges at most 200 pending symbols and retains the remainder for later sessions. Extension pages receive a separately versioned scanner artifact capped at 3 MiB with no portrait references. Catalog initialization, including a cold scanner-artifact fetch, starts only after host `load`; a cached scanner still avoids a per-tab manifest request. A retired immutable card endpoint returns `410` with `card_snapshot_retired`; only that explicit signal starts one deduplicated, cache-busted read of the existing small manifest. The recovered snapshot aborts retired requests, invalidates both projection caches, and retries the visible hover without a reload, while an unchanged scanner artifact is never downloaded again. HTML and PDF register recognized anchors with one tab-scoped reading session. Initial and mutation-driven recognition scans replace text in bounded idle slices. That session uses parallel version-addressed immutable rich-detail and compact portrait-locator GETs backed only by the same named published card artifact; the locator may deliver the portrait while rich detail stalls, has no independent publication or authority, and must agree with detail on snapshot and portrait SHA. The session inventories anchors immediately but starts speculative detail, portrait delivery resolution, bytes, decode, and persistent-frame acknowledgement only after host `load`, a one-second quiet delay, and a genuine idle callback. It prepares the first ten ordinary-document symbols with one worker on constrained connections and two otherwise; large documents use deterministic ten-symbol near-viewport working windows. Data Saver and 2G disable preparation. Hover bypasses the host-page gate, selects an already-ready card when available, and may promote matching in-flight immutable work without awaiting whole-cache hydration. Pointer-trajectory, DOM-neighbor, scroll-direction, and surface-specific prediction are forbidden. Details persist in a 4 MiB revision-keyed cache and locators in a 768 KiB revision-keyed cache without blocking paint; an older-started response from another snapshot cannot roll back a newer adopted response. Rich hover variants share one permanently mounted renderer. The shared adapter normally hydrates browser-native HTTPS sources through the IPD-001 hedge while worker-buffered data URLs are CSP compatibility only. Partial public card reads reuse bounded isolate-local caches of three parsed manifests and at most four parsed immutable shards under a 16 MiB estimated parsed-heap ceiling, with per-key in-flight deduplication; KV remains the sole authority. Administrator-owned publication aliases and the complete shared text blocklist have separate bounded D1 desired state and immutable KV staging histories, but anonymous manifest, search, and resolver paths split only the newest valid immutable recognition-pair bundle. One bounded D1 receipt binds the validator revision, scanner build, and exact alias/blocklist revision-version tuple. Catalog publication performs the full fused traversal while scanner genes are already in memory and records the exact receipt before manifest advance. Normal public recognition reads perform zero KV list operations: they GET one exact current pointer and its exact immutable pair. A missing pointer permits the legacy list scan only for first-deploy migration, and production verification must reject an absent pointer. Foreground reconciliation is list-free. Scheduled reconciliation may perform bounded best-effort cleanup after a real publication, but a no-op cycle performs no history lists.
fences.reason: The browser risk is cloning cold portrait metadata into every tab, crossing Chromium's 10 MiB storage quota, doing network, persistence, renderer boot, and decode work only after the pointer arrives, or letting eager extension work outrank the host page. Separating the compact matcher from immutable per-symbol reads preserves browser and CDN caching without restoring a portrait-heavy scanner. B-711 proved that making portrait discovery downstream of the larger rich-detail transfer lets repeated detail stalls erase an otherwise healthy portrait path; an independent compact projection of the same artifact removes that dependency without creating another canon. A document inventory is a stronger demand signal than pointer prediction, but browser-level resource priority is not created by an internal `background` label. Host-load and idle gating, cooperative DOM slices, a ten-symbol working set, and at most two speculative workers preserve ready hovers without competing with page rendering and critical assets. One shared HTML/PDF session prevents surface drift, and foreground hover bypasses the speculative gate. Data Saver/2G remain opt-out boundaries. Native HTTPS loading and a short canonical hedge avoid serial full-body probe, base64, and regional DNS-timeout costs. Parsed immutable manifest/shard reuse removes repeated KV parsing without creating another authority. Carrying both tiny administrator policies in one manifest bundle avoids a second polling path, catalog rebuilds, divergent packaged defaults, and eventually consistent KV regions exposing invalid combinations. Production Error 1102 proved that even one 1.9 MiB scanner parse plus a 19,023-gene traversal exceeds the Free Worker 10 ms CPU ceiling, so targeted immutable shards remain mandatory.

The readable marker must never carry identity or authority; anonymous recognition reads must never fall back to D1 or independently combine alias and blocklist revisions; immutable detail and locator reads must never fall back to mutable D1 state; the locator must remain a direct projection of the named card payload with the same snapshot and portrait SHA and must never acquire an independent selection or publication pointer; portrait paint must not depend on rich-detail success; disagreements must fail closed; a nonempty malformed or nonvisible pair namespace must fail closed unless an isolate has last-known-good state; bootstrap is allowed only while the pair namespace is empty; policy-only revisions must not rebuild the scanner; foreground policy mutation must never read or parse the scanner artifact; catalog publication must CAS-guard receipt creation; normal public recognition reads and foreground retries must perform zero KV list operations; missing-pointer legacy discovery is migration-only and production must always retain the exact current pointer; valid but not-yet-visible compatibility snapshots must remain retryable; portrait references must not return to the per-tab scanner map; speculative reading-session preparation must wait for host load and a genuine idle turn, never run on Data Saver or 2G, exceed ten symbols or two workers, or create a second authority; foreground hover must bypass the gate and reuse matching in-flight immutable detail and portrait work; pointer-trajectory, neighbor, scroll-direction, and surface-specific prediction must not return; worker-buffered data URLs remain a CSP compatibility fallback; and parsed card caches stay bounded, publication-version safe, and KV-authoritative. Deterministic immutable projections and byte-equivalent Bunny caches are allowed under the existing snapshot authority; the current per-gene Worker transport is an implementation, not a fence. Cache API hits still consume Worker requests.

fences.title: Iconoplasm public reads stay cold-safe inside the one loud state boundary
fences.decision: Canonical gene first paint uses a publication-owned O(1) D1 identity index with no portrait or vote fields. The route index and discovery/catalog rows establish identity and membership only. One bounded read obtains the requested exact card from the artifact selected by KV_GALLERY_VERSION, which is the sole public portrait authority; bounded current D1 reads may still supply rich detail, candidates, and votes. The complete detail response ETag and HTML cache key include the selected card version, and the HTML cache is checked before detail parsing or rendering. A valid exact card without a published portrait produces a noindex gene page, while a missing requested card or missing or invalid selected artifact produces an uncached 503. All extracted modules remain behind the existing loudly named single state owner.
fences.reason: Disposable Cloudflare isolates make process warmth an invalid correctness assumption, and treating a route or catalog portrait field as a cache or fallback authority can split first paint from the exact published card epoch. A broad refactor can also accidentally recreate the retired public-proxy topology if the protective filenames and route owner are treated as ordinary names.

Never put mutable portrait or vote state in the route index; derive or validate a public portrait from a route or discovery/catalog SHA; fall back to D1 or another card version when the selected exact card is missing; add a second Worker, public proxy, or service-binding hop for normal reads; or replace the protective prefix/suffix with a shortened responsibility-only boundary name.

fences.title: Routine gallery publication is dirty-shard-only
fences.decision: Canonical publish events prepare only their owning content-addressed card shards, in steps of at most six shards per Worker invocation, then atomically flip one manifest. Routine cron and voting paths never rebuild the complete catalog.
fences.reason: The fixed gene universe makes a complete-catalog rebuild unrelated to normal vote scope. The former scattered-delta fallback delayed visible votes, consumed avoidable KV operations, and made an exceptional migration mechanism look like ordinary publication.

Never introduce a dirty-count or shard-count threshold that falls back to complete-catalog work.

fences.title: Every public canonical blot uses one published card artifact
fences.decision: The exact versioned card artifact selected by KV_GALLERY_VERSION owns the selected source portrait and every input used to derive its canonical workstation-materialized blot fingerprint and immutable Bunny key. Discovery, catalog, D1, and account rows may establish identity, membership, ordering, rich detail, candidates, audit status, and authoring or vote state, but their portrait references are never public image authority. Signed-in and anonymous card views render the blot composition from the exact card VM; the stable public blot route derives its expected object directly from that VM and does not require a blot-only KV publication. The extension portrait locator is a read-time projection of the same named card payload with no independent selection, pointer, version, or publication timeline. Byte-equivalent CDN caches and deterministic immutable projections are allowed under that same authority. Gene-page standard images and metadata, structured data, image-sitemap children, public media, and search-image retrieval use the matching immutable blot WebP. Massive gene-range pages remain text-only. Every derived cache and ETag includes the selected card version. Missing exact-card state fails closed. A complete card without uploaded current bytes remains an indexable gene profile and sitemap/archive member; the temporary source portrait remains separately typed until all 19,023 current blot objects are proven accessible.
fences.reason: The former account image-only path used the separately versioned publishedPortraitRefs snapshot and caused B-700. The same split recurs if a gene page, sitemap, or public media response reads a raw D1 portrait or if search metadata treats a source portrait as the finished blot. One exact card barrier plus a deterministic visible-material fingerprint keeps every projection in the same portrait-selection epoch while eliminating roughly 19,000 unnecessary KV backfill writes.

A replacement must prove D1 or catalog drift cannot change the published source or blot, detail and locator agree on snapshot and portrait SHA, page, sitemap, and public media agree with the selected card version and blot SHA, and the signed-in homepage and gene page visually match in one browser session.

fences.title: Daily targets give every gene surname one slot
fences.decision: Automatic GeneGuessr daily selection walks a deterministic without-replacement shuffle-bag of normalized gene surnames and chooses one deterministic representative per surname. Automatic targets cannot repeat inside one complete playable-surname cycle. Manual overrides and recorded availability replacements remain explicit exceptions.
fences.reason: Hashing across the flat protein table makes large families proportionally more likely. The surname-balancing schema and practice selector existed, but daily mode bypassed them and automatically selected SLC22A5, SLC6A8, and SLC12A2 in July 2026.

Never restore flat-table weighting, independent per-date hashing, or adjacent-row fallback.

fences.title: Recap images require pixel and storage proof
fences.decision: A GeneGuessr recap image is publishable only after the browser proves stable molecule pixels and object storage returns the exact uploaded bytes from the immutable day, UniProt, and renderer identity. Missing images preserve the text recap; repairs edit the recorded Discord message in place. Annual coverage is a resumable reconciliation: bounded preflight and final reads, skip verified objects, group missing days by protein, retain one bitmap at a time, and report success only for 365/365 exact objects.
fences.reason: The July renderer uploaded a uniform dark canvas that Discord displayed as a blank attachment. The August Bunny cutover then accepted an upload response without proving the object existed, so NHP2 posted without an attachment while the admin UI reported success and its startup warning crashed before schedule initialization. B-702 then found only 1 of 365 yearly objects ready and proved the old bulk button had no checkpoint, skip-ready behavior, memory bound, or exact final audit.

Never treat attachment presence, a generic 2xx, object metadata, an attempted-upload count, or non-zero byte length as proof that a visible protein will reach Discord.

fences.title: Remote prose checks are explicit, snapshot-bound, and free-Zen-only
fences.decision: Harper grammar may run locally after editor idle, while DeepSeek prose agents run only after an explicit user command against one immutable complete-document snapshot. Remote startup and typing paths read no credential and send no traffic. The sole remote model is deepseek-v4-flash-free on OpenCode Zen, with no paid, Go, or alternate-provider fallback.
fences.reason: Whole-document atomic agents take roughly one to two minutes apiece and duplicate private prose across requests. A live trigger would race edits, flood the provider, worsen Obsidian startup, and send drafts without deliberate consent. A silent fallback could convert expiry of the free preview into unbounded paid use.

Any replacement must preserve explicit initiation, immutable full-document snapshots, exact one-error agents, and fail-closed cost behavior.
